drawings.notes: The system X -> A^1_{X/S}, Pic^0_{X/S} <- Pic^0_{A^1/S} = Pic^0_{A^0/S} with the brace on its left, and under it the upward arrow B -> Pic^0_{X/S} and the oblique arrow from Pic^0_{A^1/S} down towards B, crossed by a short stroke. The page ends below.

drawings.description: en marge, un petit tableau incliné, à colonnes, où se lisent $\mathrm{Div}^+$ et quelques mots illisibles
drawings.notes: Tilted frame, its corners computed once: the top edge from the top left corner to the top right corner (broken where a word crosses it, as on the page), the right edge down to the bottom right corner, the bottom edge curving back to the bottom left corner, the left edge (which starts only below the first row on the page; the short stroke above it is drawn apart); the inner bottom line ending at the bottom right corner. Four column lines, the first ending on the bottom edge. The heavy stroke across the two right columns is drawn. Div^+ placed where "Div" is visible in the lower right cell, along his writing. Still differs: the other words in the cells (x+, f, +x and the like) are not legible enough to be composed and are left out; the two right column lines are approximate (faint and partly overwritten). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): laid over the scan rendered at 400 dpi in colour, whole and zoomed (10-16 px a unit); not compiled (no TeX engine in the session), the TikZ was rasterised by a script; nothing changed. The frame (its broken top edge, the right edge, the bottom curve, the left edge and the short stroke above it), the inner bottom line and the heavy stroke across the two right columns lie on their ink within about 1 to 2 units. Kept partial: the four column lines are straight lines between approximate ends, while on the page they are faint, slightly curved and partly overwritten by the words in the cells; in their middle they leave the ink by up to about 5 units (the first two most), and which faint stroke continues which is not certain; the words in the cells are not legible and are left out (Div^+ only is set).

drawings.description: dans la boucle du diagramme, une tête coiffée d'un chapeau à large bord
drawings.kind: doodle: head with a wide-brimmed hat
drawings.notes: Overinked doodle in the loop of the diagram: the thick closed outline (the brim of the hat, or the loop passing round the head) traced along the middle of the ink; inside, the face: an upper bar, a short vertical stroke under it, a lower bar, and the lower part filled (drawn as a heavy band). The two lines of the diagram reaching it from the left end on the outline. Still differs: the ink is very heavy and the width of the outline and the filled lower part are only suggested; the faint third stroke at the lower left is left out. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): redrawn on a millimetre grid of the scan rendered at 400 dpi in colour (10 px a unit); not compiled (no TeX engine in the session), the TikZ was rasterised by a script and laid over the crop; every stroke lies on its ink within about 1 unit. The ring is one stroke 5.5 units wide along the middle of his band (5 to 7 units wide on the page), through seventeen points read on it, so that its width is drawn and not only suggested; inside, the upper bar, the short upright and the lower bar at their weights, and the dark hump at the bottom of the window filled (the two horizontal bands drawn before are not on the page). The two lines from the left re-read: the lower one bends back down to the left (the « faint third stroke » is this bend). Left out: the heavy curve that leaves the ring at the lower right and runs down out of the crop (the loop of the diagram, not the doodle).

drawings.description: figure : les composantes $X_i$, $X_j$ découpées dans $X$ par des arcs, $Y_i$ et $Y_j$ portés sur elles, $X_{ij}$ et $Z_{ij}$ marqués au point d'intersection, avec flèches vers les étiquettes
drawings.kind: components of a scheme cut by arcs
drawings.notes: Strokes meeting at one computed point each: the heavy point P, from which run the short strokes to the left and to the lower right, the stroke down to the lower left corner C1, the arc coming from the upper left (Y_i side), the long curve to the upper right and the stroke to the right towards the label Y_j; from C1 the lower arc to the right corner R1 (which rises to the top right) and the curve down to the bottom; the long stroke from the top crossing everything down to its corner K, which turns back to the lower left; the separate line at the upper left. On the right, the heavy vertical stroke and the narrow wedge. Arrows: the curved arrow from X, the arrows towards P from Y_i, from X_ij down to the crossing, the arrowhead before Y_j, the arrow from the right. Labels at \small after the transcription, where the letters stand: X, Y_i, X_ij, Y_j, Z_ij, and "ij)" under P. Still differs: which piece is X_i and which X_j cannot be told, so neither is written; the reading of the two right-hand labels (Y_j, Z_ij) and of the top left X (perhaps X_i) follows the earlier redraw and the transcription, not a clear reading of the page; the heavy vertical on the right may be part of a label. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Revised 2026-11-09 after Michel's check (#135): yes, the labels are right as drawn (X, Y_i, X_ij, Y_j, Z_ij, ij)), after the transcription; ok.

drawings.description: à gauche, deux petits diagrammes : $Z \xrightarrow{i} X$, $Z$ fermé, avec $f \colon X \to S$ et $\varphi \colon Z \to S$ ; et le triangle $X \to \Sigma \to S$, $X \to S$ ; un troisième croquis du même triangle, isolé au bas de la page
drawings.notes: Upper: the triangle X -> Sigma -> S with X -> S, arrows as he drew them (heavy heads), the Sigma written sideways. Lower: Z, the inclusion sign with a small mark above it (read i by the transcription, a "?" on the crop), X; f: X -> S upwards; phi: Z -> S as a thin oblique arrow; the word "fermé" to the left of Z. Labels at \small. Left out, as not part of the figure: the two long pencil lines crossing the lower right of the crop, which frame the lines of text written upside down on the lower half of the page (the sheet turned), the horizontal rule of that text, and the mirror text showing through from the back. The third sketch of the triangle mentioned by the transcription is not within this crop and is not drawn here. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: cinq segments de droite se coupant deux à deux en formant un pentagone
drawings.kind: five lines forming a pentagon (cycle of components)
drawings.notes: Five line segments, each crossing its two neighbours, forming a pentagon (a cycle in the combinatorial scheme of C). Not encoded: a cycle of five rational components with no legs is not a stable graph, and no other schema fits.

drawings.description: page de croquis de courbes stables : configurations de composantes rationnelles (traits) se coupant transversalement, l'une marquée $g$ ; une autre à deux composantes marquées $g'$ et $g''$, avec
drawings.kind: sketches of stable curves (configurations of lines)
drawings.notes: Three sketches, every stroke read on a tight crop. Top: three crossing lines and a fourth line marked g, crossed by two short strokes. Middle left: three crossing strokes, and below them a star of three lines through the heavy point, the three drawn through the same computed point. Right: three crossing strokes; under them a long line crossed by three strokes, the last of which runs down out of the group, with g'' (above that stroke) and g' (at the end of the long line). Labels at \small, where he wrote them. The formula g' + g'' = g (g', g'' > 0) to the right is text, in the transcription. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: une chaîne de composantes rationnelles marquée $g = 0$, avec « $(g = 0$ » ; un ovale ; un arc portant des points épaissis, accompagné de croix ; plusieurs étoiles de droites concourantes ; un pentagone de droites marqué de points ; deux lettres $k$ isolées
drawings.kind: page of sketches of stable curves
drawings.notes: Redrawn group by group from two tight crops placed back into the page crop. Top right: three crossing strokes, the chain - a long line crossed by three strokes and ending in a blot (drawn as a point) - with g = 0 (overwritten) and "(g = 0" further right. Lower left: the thick arc with two heavy end points crossed by thin strokes meeting near its lower part; the second thick arc carrying three thickened points, with the three small crosses beside it; the two letters k. Lower middle: the oval (doubled stroke); three crossing lines with the mark "1" and two small ticks; the pentagon of five lines with its four points. Right: the two stars of concurrent lines (each drawn through one computed centre, with a heavy point there) and the strokes crossing them. Labels at \small. Still differs: the strokes of the dense right-hand group are read stroke by stroke but several are faint and overlapping, so their number and ends are approximate; in the left star the thin strokes do not quite meet in one point on the page and are drawn as he drew them; the sketches at the top left of the page are those of 08-3. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Revised 2026-11-09 after Michel's check (#135): yes, as redrawn; the strokes of the dense sketch groups are accepted as drawn, so the figure is set ok.

A loop with a double point: the long stroke (doubled at its top) runs down through the heavy double point, the loop leaves it and closes back on it, and two short strokes cross the loop on the right. Three crossing lines. Two lines through two heavy points: one line through both points, one through the upper point (ending in a hook), one through the lower point; the mark "1" at the upper right. A heavy point; from it two branches leave to the right with a common tangent (on the page they run together as one thick stroke for about a tenth of the width), then part, one rising, one falling. Both curves start at the same computed point with the same tangent. The faint « k[t]/t^2 » to the left of the sketch is text and is not drawn. Nothing struck. drawings.description: dans la marge gauche, une figure en éventail : quatre triangles adjacents partant d'un même sommet, coupés par un arc
drawings.kind: fan of triangles cut by an arc
drawings.notes: Bbox widened to take the whole of the long stroke. Two triangles with the common vertex V, drawn on computed corners: the upper one V-A-B opening to the right (on the page its sides stop just short of V and A; joined), the lower one V-C-D pointing up, its base slightly bowed. The long, almost straight pencil stroke runs down the margin through the lower left corner C and on below the figure. The scribble at the top left and the formulas on the right are text and are not drawn. Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Revised 2026-11-09 after Michel's check (#136): the drawing is right, there are two triangles; the transcription's « quatre triangles » is the reading to correct there (see disagreement).
drawings.disagreement: The transcription reads four adjacent triangles from one vertex; the page shows two (the upper one opening to the right, the lower one pointing up), sharing that vertex. Michel confirmed two (#136, 2026-11-09).
